notes: Second daf of the bounded 79b-88a campaign. Fresh reconstruction of all 65 raw Rashi lines, the densest daf handled so far in this campaign. Prior content was fabricated in layers: vl1-5 were generic thematic mis-summaries with no basis in the raw Hebrew (e.g. vl1 claimed 'all Torah eating measures equal an egg-bulk except Yom Kippur's date-bulk,' a claim actually contradicted by the raw text, which opens by stating all measures are an olive-bulk EXCEPT the impurity of foods; vl2-3 invented a gezerah-shavah-to-matzah theory found nowhere in the actual Rashi); vl6-48 (43 lines) were pure repeated boilerplate across three filler strings, exactly the entries drained in this PR; vl49-64 already carried a genuine, accurate translation matching the raw Hebrew closely and were largely preserved (only lightly retranslated for consistency with the rest of the daf and to add missing links); vl65 was a meta-description replaced with the honest truncated translation. Rebuilt/relinked all 65 entries against the raw Hebrew and the 16-id local segment table across three sugyot: yoma-080a-s01 (Egg-Bulk as the Universal Eating Measure, l01/l05), yoma-080a-s02 (Deriving the YK Eating Measure by Gezerah Shavah, l07 through l31), yoma-080a-s03 (The Cheekful: YK Drinking Measure, l36 through l46). Two local segments (l25 and l36) have no Rashi comment on this daf and are left unused: l25 is the Gemara's own rejected 'small olive-bulk' hypothesis, explained by its own wording and superseded before Rashi comments further; l36 is the Mishnah's cheekful teaching, which the Gemara immediately reinterprets on its own ('eima: kemlo lugmav') before Rashi's commentary resumes at the Beit Hillel/Beraita challenge (l40/l43). This is expected: not every local segment requires a comment. Many genuine multi-id dual-links were used at confirmed DH-transition seams throughout this dense daf (vl5, vl10, vl34, vl37, vl38, vl45, vl48, vl52, vl54, vl60, vl61, vl62, vl63), each verified by direct textual continuity: either the trailing word of one Rashi comment completing a citation/phrase that belongs to the prior segment while the next word begins a new dibbur quoting the next segment's own opening phrase (e.g. vl37 ends '...robo' finishing the Rabbi Abbahu/l14 discussion, then ': ha'ochel chelev' begins a new comment quoting l17's own opening words), or a single densely-printed line covering two or three short dibburim in sequence (vl61-63, where 'Yaavetz', 'kama yishteh', and the textual note on 'ika beinaihu kemlo lugmav dachuk' each get their own brief gloss within one printed line, correctly split across l28/l31, l31/l40/l43, and l43/l46 respectively). None of these are positional guesses: each is grounded in either a direct quoted phrase matching the target segment's own text, or confirmed grammatical continuity into the following vilna line. vl1 opens a fresh comment (no continuation from 79b, which ended with its own truncated word already linked forward). The truncated final line (vl65, a single word 'ki') was checked against 80b's actual raw Rashi opening (confirmed by reading modules/yoma/assets/talmuddev/80b.json, which opens 'ki itshil. bevei midrasha hach dele'eil kama yishteh...' - 'when it was asked, in the study hall, this question above about how much one must drink...'), directly continuing the same Beit Hillel/Beit Shammai cheekful discussion, and stays linked to l46 as the daf's final segment. All 65 English strings are distinct. Multi-anchor-safe evidence tier: the drift-profile scanner reports classification ALIGNED, 5 of 5 expected anchors found, 0 missing. Four of the five anchors are at offset 0 (the Chullin 74a and Bekhorot 57b same-line citations, and the Berakhot tractate-name half of the Berakhot 39a citation). The fifth anchor (the '39a' daf-number half of that same citation) is at offset +1 and flagged splitContinuation by the drift-profile tooling fix landed in this campaign's second tooling PR (#114): the raw Hebrew itself splits this citation across two print lines (raw line 50 ends '(Berakhot', raw line 51 opens '39a) that...'), and the English mirrors that same honest split, so the daf-number naturally lands one line later. This is a source-grounded structural artifact, not translation drift, and the tooling fix's own regression tests confirm the review gate now correctly distinguishes this from a real misalignment. No citation was invented, moved, or duplicated in the rebuild. The 43 allowlist-drain snapshot entries (vl6-48) are all now genuinely fixed by this rebuild and were validator-confirmed stale (validate_rashi_content.py --json reported all 43 vilnaLines stale) before being removed in this same PR, per the allowlist-drain workflow (PR #106).
